back: A material whose properties change in response to an external stimulus such as temperature, light, pressure or electrical current.
An alloy that returns to a pre-set shape when heated after being deformed. The most common is Nitinol (nickel + titanium).
Spectacle frames that return to shape when warmed, dental braces that gently move teeth at body temperature, and medical stents that expand inside the body.
A thermoplastic that softens and becomes mouldable at about 62°C (in hot water), sets rigid when cool, and can be reheated and reshaped many times.
Custom handles and grips, small prototypes, prosthetic components and model-making in D&T.
Change colour when exposed to ultraviolet (UV) light and return to their original colour when the UV is removed.
Transition spectacle lenses, security printing on banknotes and documents, and UV-reactive inks.
Change colour in response to temperature; the change is reversible.
Baby spoons, bottles and bath thermometers that show a safe temperature, mood rings, and food and drink packaging that shows serving temperature.
Enclosing tiny particles or droplets in a coating that releases its contents when broken by pressure, heat or friction.
Scratch-and-sniff products, phase-change textiles that regulate body temperature, antibacterial fabrics and self-healing materials.
Technology that identifies or authenticates people using unique biological characteristics — fingerprints, face, iris or voice.
Personal biological data is highly sensitive, so its storage and use must be carefully regulated.
Fibres woven into fabric that carry electrical signals — used in heated jackets, wearable technology and sports performance monitoring.
Fibres woven into garments that change shape or tighten in response to temperature or moisture.
